events.context: Identifies user's key admission as not knowing what they want, root of all problems
Breaks down user's internal conflict into four voices: A (intimacy), B (freedom), C (injured child), D (proud adult)
Explains indecision stems from not wanting to choose, leading to exhaustion
Analyzes why she left: saw user's refusal to choose, her three demands forced decision
Instructs user to self-reflect with three questions on paper or notes app about desired life, sacrifices, regret
Her statement 'I’m not gonna deal with your issues' interpreted as forcing user's choice
User's response 'I don’t want to choose, don’t force me?' with 'lol' as cold laugh
Her response mirrors user's logic satirically, summarizing his messages as 'I don’t want to choose, don’t force me'
Presents two paths: 1. Admit not wanting to choose and end; 2. Admit fear and choose with true statements like 'I’m afraid'
Challenges user to prove her wrong by choosing or admit she's right
Text transitions to Anthropic announcement of Project Glasswing
Announces Project Glasswing with partners: AWS, Anthropic, Apple, etc., to secure critical software using Claude Mythos Preview
Model finds thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities in OSes, browsers; examples: OpenBSD 27-year-old vuln, FFmpeg 16-year-old, Linux kernel chain
Commits $100M usage credits, $4M donations; shares learnings; extends access to 40+ orgs
Quotes from Cisco, AWS, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Linux Foundation, JPMorganChase, Google, Palo Alto Networks endorsing project
Shows Mythos Preview superior scores on CyberGym (83.1%), SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, GPQA, etc., vs. Opus 4.6
Outlines future: access at $25/$125 per M tokens, donations, reports in 90 days, collaborations on standards, govt discussions
